meta.title: Who keeps the canal alive?
meta.standfirst: On a stretch of the Rochdale Canal, a dozen volunteers spend their Saturdays pulling trolleys, traffic cones and shopping bags out of the water. *Why do they keep coming back?*
meta.seoTitle: Who keeps the canal alive? Volunteers on the Rochdale Canal
meta.seoDescription: Every Saturday, volunteers clear rubbish from a stretch of the Rochdale Canal. A sample feature for testing the Galley runtime.
meta.shareText: Meet the volunteers who clear the canal every week.

data.body:
It is 9am on a wet Saturday, and Rita Okafor is already up to her elbows in the Rochdale Canal.
"You'd be amazed what people throw in," she says, hauling a **bicycle wheel** onto the towpath. "Last month we found a safe. Empty, before you ask."
The group meets every week near Ancoats. Most members found it by accident: a poster in a café, a friend of a friend, a walk that ended with someone handing them a litter-picker.
This is a sample story for testing. People, places and sources are invented.

## A slow, muddy kind of care
Volunteering on waterways has grown since the pandemic, according to a regional survey (Hughes 2021). Members describe three reasons for joining:
- the *visible* result at the end of a session;
- the company;
- a sense that the canal belongs to them.
For background on the canal's history, see [the Rochdale Canal entry on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochdale_Canal).
### What they find
1. Shopping trolleys, usually two or three a month.
2. Traffic cones.
3. Plastic bottles, by the hundred.

data.text: Nobody asked us to do this. That's sort of the point.
